title: The Latino Voters Who Could Decide the Midterms

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ，你每晚也要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，然后你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Latino voters have never seemed more electorally important or more up for grabs than in the midterm elections next month that will determine whether Democrats or Republicans
sentences.zh: 在下个月的中期选举中，拉丁裔选民似乎从未像现在这样在选举中显得如此重要，也从未像现在这样摇摆不定，而这次选举将决定民主党还是共和党

sentences.en: control Congress.
sentences.zh: 控制国会。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: My colleague, Jennifer Medina, on what a Times poll and a series of follow-up interviews for The Daily has revealed about how those voters see both parties.
sentences.zh: 我的同事詹妮弗·梅迪纳将为我们解读《每日新闻》的一项民意调查及后续系列采访，揭示这些选民如何看待两大政党。

sentences.en: It's Monday, October 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月3日，星期一。

sentences.en: Jenny, you and our colleagues just conducted a major poll of Latino voters in the United States.
sentences.zh: 珍妮，你和我们的同事刚刚对美国的拉丁裔选民进行了一次大规模民意调查。

sentences.en: And the reason why, no doubt, is that it's an enormously consequential voting bloc in an enormously consequential election.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，原因在于这是一个在极其重要的选举中拥有巨大影响力的投票群体。

sentences.en: The first real referendum on the Biden era of government.
sentences.zh: 这是对拜登政府执政时期的第一次真正公投。

sentences.en: The first time voters across the country are going to go to the polls since Donald Trump lost the White House.
sentences.zh: 这是唐纳德·特朗普失去白宫后，全国选民首次前往投票站投票。

sentences.en: So I want to start by asking you to quantify, if you can, the role that Latino voters are expected to play in these consequential midterMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我想先请你量化一下，如果可以的话，拉丁裔选民在这些关键的中期选举中预计将发挥什么作用。

sentences.en: So Latino voters will play a huge role in deciding both the House and the Senate and control over Congress.
sentences.zh: 拉丁裔选民将在决定众议院和参议院的归属以及国会控制权方面发挥巨大作用。

sentences.en: In two of the most consequential Senate races,
sentences.zh: 在两场最关键的参议院竞选中，

sentences.en: Nevada and Arizona,
sentences.zh: 内华达州和亚利桑那州，

sentences.en: Latinos make up 20% of registered voters there.
sentences.zh: 拉丁裔占当地注册选民的20%。

sentences.en: And in the House races, this is pretty unusual.
sentences.zh: 而在众议院的竞选中，这种情况相当罕见。

sentences.en: Latinos make up more than 20% of more than a dozen competitive House races.
sentences.zh: 在十几个竞争激烈的众议院选区中，拉丁裔占比超过了20%。

sentences.en: Now, it's not unusual, of course, for Latinos to make up a big pool of voters in House races, but in competitive races, that's a relatively new phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 当然，拉丁裔在众议院选举中占有很大比例并不罕见，但在竞争激烈的选区中，这还是一个相对较新的现象。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So is this just a geographical coincidence this election year, or is there something about the fact that these districts have so many Latino voters that makes them so competitive?
sentences.zh: 那么，这仅仅是选举年的地理巧合，还是说这些选区因为有如此多的拉丁裔选民，才使得竞争如此激烈？

sentences.en: It's really a little bit of both.
sentences.zh: 两者都有一些原因。

sentences.en: The basic dynamic is that most of these districts were not competitive before.
sentences.zh: 基本动态是，这些选区中的大多数以前竞争并不激烈。

sentences.en: They were either blue districts or red rural districts.
sentences.zh: 它们要么是深蓝选区，要么是深红的农村选区。

sentences.en: And now they've been redrawn to include more Latinos.
sentences.zh: 而现在，选区划分被重新调整，纳入了更多的拉丁裔。

sentences.en: And so the addition of those Latino voters has made these districts much more purple and more competitive.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些拉丁裔选民的加入使得这些选区变得更加“紫色”，竞争也更加激烈。

sentences.en: And again, that's happened in some really key races.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这种情况发生在一些非常关键的竞选中。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: So it's not at all a stretch, given that math you just described, to say that Latino voters could very well determine which party controls both chambers of Congress in November.
sentences.zh: 所以，考虑到你刚才描述的这些数据，说拉丁裔选民很可能决定11月份哪个党派控制国会两院，这完全不是夸大其词。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Not at all a stretch.
sentences.zh: 一点也不夸张。

sentences.en: And really one of the first times it's been so clear that that is possible.
sentences.zh: 这确实是第一次如此清晰地表明这种可能性。

sentences.en: And Jenny, you've talked a lot in the past about the history of the Latino vote in the United States and bad assumptions that both parties have made about this group of voters.
sentences.zh: 珍妮，你过去经常谈论美国拉丁裔投票的历史，以及两大政党对这一选民群体所做的错误假设。

sentences.en: And just remind us of that.
sentences.zh: 请提醒我们一下。

sentences.en: As you all began to undertake this poll, what's the understanding that existed of the Latino vote?
sentences.zh: 当你们开始进行这项民意调查时，人们对拉丁裔选民的认知是怎样的？

sentences.en: Well, that's really the other reason why we decided to do this poll, because our understanding had gone so topsy-turvy over the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实是我们决定进行这项民意调查的另一个原因，因为在过去10年里，我们的认知已经变得天翻地覆。

sentences.en: When you look back at 2012,
sentences.zh: 当你回顾2012年时，

sentences.en: Barack Obama had a huge, record-breaking number of Latino support.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马获得了创纪录的巨大拉丁裔支持。

sentences.en: And so speculation after 2012 was this is the new
sentences.zh: 所以2012年之后的猜测是，这就是新的

sentences.en: Democratic majority.
sentences.zh: 民主党多数派。

sentences.en: Democrats are going to have a permanent majority, largely because of Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 民主党将拥有永久的多数席位，很大程度上是因为拉丁裔选民。

sentences.en: When Republicans lost in November, it was a wake-up call.
sentences.zh: 当共和党在11月落败时，这是一个警钟。

sentences.en: The Republicans are so freaked out that they do this huge study and basically come away with this message.
sentences.zh: 共和党人非常恐慌，以至于他们做了这项大规模的研究，并基本得出了这样的结论。

sentences.en: The way we communicate our principles isn't resonating widely enough.
sentences.zh: 我们传达原则的方式没有引起足够广泛的共鸣。

sentences.en: We'll never, ever win unless we do better with Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 除非我们在拉丁裔选民身上做得更好，否则我们永远、永远不会赢。

sentences.en: Focus groups described our party as narrow-minded, out-of-touch, and, quote, stuffy old men.
sentences.zh: 焦点小组将我们的党描述为思想狭隘、脱离现实，以及，引用原话，“老古板”。

sentences.en: We've got to change our message on immigration.
sentences.zh: 我们必须改变我们在移民问题上的信息。

sentences.en: We've got to change our message on diversity.
sentences.zh: 我们必须改变我们在多元化问题上的信息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Then four years later...
sentences.zh: 然后四年后……

sentences.en: I would build a great wall, and nobody builds walls better than me, believe me.
sentences.zh: 我会建一堵伟大的墙，没有人比我更擅长建墙，相信我。

sentences.en: ...comes Donald Trump with his anti-immigrant message.
sentences.zh: ……唐纳德·特朗普带着他的反移民信息出现了。

sentences.en: They're bringing drugs.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了毒品。

sentences.en: They're bringing crime.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了犯罪。

sentences.en: They're rapists.
sentences.zh: 他们是强奸犯。

sentences.en: Right, breaking all of the rules that Republicans said they were going to start to follow after 2012.
sentences.zh: 没错，打破了共和党人声称在2012年后要开始遵守的所有规则。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Democrats think, we don't really need to go after Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 而民主党人认为，我们真的不需要去争取拉丁裔选民。

sentences.en: Donald Trump is repelling them for us.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普正在为我们把他们推开。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, of course, in 2020...
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，在2020年……

sentences.en: It's going to be one of the big surprises, I think, you see that come out of 2020, and the Democrats are going to be really confused by it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这将是2020年出现的一大惊喜，民主党人对此会感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: President Trump receiving
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统获得了

sentences.en: 35% of the Hispanic vote this year, up seven points from 2016.
sentences.zh: 今年35%的西班牙裔选票，比2016年上升了7个百分点。

sentences.en: We see Latino voters moving toward Donald Trump in a way that really shocks most of the political world.
sentences.zh: 我们看到拉丁裔选民以一种让大多数政治界人士感到震惊的方式转向唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Democrats are now being warned.
sentences.zh: 民主党人现在受到了警告。

sentences.en: That shift is only growing.
sentences.zh: 这种转变只会加剧。

sentences.en: And then there had become this sort of conventional wisdom that that had started this sort of mass exodus among Latino voters from the Democratic Party toward the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 然后出现了一种普遍的共识，认为这开启了拉丁裔选民从民主党向共和党的大规模出走。

sentences.en: And that there was just a continual march toward conservatism within Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 而且拉丁裔选民内部有一种持续向保守主义靠拢的趋势。

sentences.en: One of the big questions in 2022 is, is that going to continue?
sentences.zh: 2022年的一个大问题是，这种情况会持续吗？

sentences.en: Could that accelerate?
sentences.zh: 这会加速吗？

sentences.en: Will that scramble midterm politics?
sentences.zh: 这会扰乱中期选举的政治格局吗？

sentences.en: So just to summarize that, as you undertake this poll, our understanding of Latino voters is that we don't really understand them.
sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，当你们进行这项民意调查时，我们对拉丁裔选民的理解就是我们并不真正了解他们。

sentences.en: And the questions that everyone seems to be asking are, are Latino voters naturally Democrats or were they once naturally Democrats but now they are
sentences.zh: 每个人似乎都在问的问题是，拉丁裔选民天生就是民主党人，还是他们曾经天生是民主党人，但现在他们正在

sentences.en: moving from the Democratic Party over to the Republican Party?
sentences.zh: 从民主党转向共和党？

sentences.en: This is a very confusing moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人困惑的时刻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a very confusing moment and there's sort of a collective what is going on here.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人困惑的时刻，大家都在集体纳闷这里到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And when in doubt, do a poll.
sentences.zh: 当有疑问时，就做个民意调查。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So given all of that, what does this poll find?
sentences.zh: 那么考虑到所有这些，这项民意调查发现了什么？

sentences.en: So that big question that we wanted to know, are Latino voters fleeing the Democratic Party and flocking toward Republicans?
sentences.zh: 所以我们想知道的那个大问题是，拉丁裔选民是否正在逃离民主党并涌向共和党？

sentences.en: The answer to that is no.
sentences.zh: 答案是否定的。

sentences.en: Most Hispanic voters, more than 50%, say they will vote for Democrats this fall.
sentences.zh: 大多数西班牙裔选民，超过50%，表示他们今年秋天会投票给民主党。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: And roughly 30% say they will vote for Republicans, which is about in line with what's happened historically.
sentences.zh: 大约30%的人表示他们会投票给共和党，这与历史上的情况大致相符。

sentences.en: And why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: Well, what the poll showed is really this belief that Democrats are the party of the working class is part of what's keeping
sentences.zh: 嗯，民意调查显示，这种认为民主党是工人阶级政党的信念，正是让

sentences.en: Latino voters committed to that party.
sentences.zh: 拉丁裔选民忠于该党的部分原因。

sentences.en: And the support is driven largely by women and partly by older voters.
sentences.zh: 这种支持主要由女性和部分老年选民推动。

sentences.en: And overall, you see Hispanic voters agreeing with Democrats on a whole bunch of issues.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，你会看到西班牙裔选民在很多问题上与民主党达成共识。

sentences.en: Immigration, gun policy, climate.
sentences.zh: 移民、枪支政策、气候。

sentences.en: There are lots of reasons that they still feel committed to the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然忠于民主党的原因有很多。

sentences.en: But all of that said, there's some huge warning signs, flashing red lights for Democrats and openings for Republicans both now and years from now.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，对于民主党来说，这确实有一些巨大的警告信号，闪烁的红灯，以及现在和未来几年共和党人的机会。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, let's focus on that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们关注这一点。

sentences.en: The vulnerability of Democrats that has been revealed by this poll and the opportunity that it tells us exists for Republicans because that dynamic seems to be very consequential
sentences.zh: 这项民意调查揭示了民主党的脆弱性，以及它告诉我们共和党人所拥有的机会，因为这种动态似乎非常重要

sentences.en: in these House and Senate races that you mentioned earlier, Jenny, because it could tip the scales, right?
sentences.zh: 在珍妮你刚才提到的那些众议院和参议院竞选中，因为它可能会扭转局面，对吧？

sentences.en: If Republicans lure even more
sentences.zh: 如果共和党人吸引了比2020年更多的

sentences.en: Latino voters than they did in 2020, they may have a very good midterm.
sentences.zh: 拉丁裔选民，他们可能会在中期选举中表现得非常好。

sentences.en: If Democrats can keep those voters or even win back Latino voters from Republicans, they will have a very good midterm.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人能够留住这些选民，甚至从共和党人手中赢回拉丁裔选民，他们就会在中期选举中表现得非常好。

sentences.en: So how should we think about that dynamic given the results of the poll?
sentences.zh: 那么考虑到民意调查的结果，我们应该如何看待这种动态？

sentences.en: So there are three broad areas where Democrats are really vulnerable and Republicans really have an opening.
sentences.zh: 民主党确实脆弱，而共和党确实有突破口的领域大致有三个。

sentences.en: And the first of those is the economy.
sentences.zh: 首先是经济。

sentences.en: So the poll showed us very clearly that Latino voters overwhelmingly consider the economy the most important issue and the most important issue deciding their vote.
sentences.zh: 民意调查非常清楚地向我们表明，拉丁裔选民绝大多数认为经济是最重要的问题，也是决定他们投票的最重要问题。

sentences.en: And when you ask which party they favor on economic issues, they're actually very split.
sentences.zh: 当你问他们在经济问题上更倾向于哪个政党时，他们的意见实际上非常分歧。

sentences.en: and almost as many voters prefer the Republican Party on economic issues as they do the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 几乎同样多的选民在经济问题上更倾向于共和党，而不是民主党。

sentences.en: That's really interesting because there's kind of an over-representation of Latinos who trust
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为在信任

sentences.en: Republicans on the economy relative to the number of Latino voters who just favor
sentences.zh: 共和党经济政策的拉丁裔选民中，存在一种过度代表性，相对于那些仅仅支持

sentences.en: Republicans in general.
sentences.zh: 共和党的拉丁裔选民总数而言。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In other words, there are people who say that they favor Democrats in general but still say they favor the Republicans on economic policy and say that the economic policy
sentences.zh: 换句话说，有些人说他们总体上支持民主党，但仍然说他们在经济政策上支持共和党，并说经济政策

sentences.en: is the most important thing determining their vote.
sentences.zh: 是决定他们投票的最重要因素。

sentences.en: So it's a huge opening for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 所以这对共和党人来说是一个巨大的突破口。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi, is this Dani?
sentences.zh: 嗨，是丹妮吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so to understand this better, we called up some of the people who responded to the poll.
sentences.zh: 为了更好地理解这一点，我们给一些参与民意调查的人打了电话。

sentences.en: Do you have a few minutes to talk now?
sentences.zh: 你现在有几分钟时间聊聊吗？

sentences.en: We just wanted to follow.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想跟进一下。

sentences.en: So take, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以，以……为例，

sentences.en: Dani Bernal.
sentences.zh: 丹妮·伯纳尔。

sentences.en: Okay, so my name is Dani Bernal.
sentences.zh: 好的，我叫丹妮·伯纳尔。
我35岁，

sentences.en: born in Bolivia, raised in Miami, and now I'm living in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 出生在玻利维亚，在迈阿密长大，现在住在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: And Dani, tell me how you think of yourself politically.
sentences.zh: 丹妮，告诉我你是如何在政治上定位自己的。

sentences.en: How do you describe yourself as a voter?
sentences.zh: 你如何描述自己作为一名选民？

sentences.en: I want to say that even though
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，尽管

sentences.en: I'm registered as a Republican,
sentences.zh: 我注册为共和党人，

sentences.en: I'm more independent because I constantly swing back and forth on issues.
sentences.zh: 但我更倾向于独立，因为我在各种问题上不断摇摆。

sentences.en: When did you register as a Republican?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候注册为共和党人的？

sentences.en: Oh, that was when I was really young, as soon as I was able to pre-register when I got my license.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是我很小的时候，拿到驾照后一能预注册我就注册了。

sentences.en: So I literally just asked my mom, like, what's the difference?
sentences.zh: 所以我当时直接问我妈妈，区别是什么？

sentences.en: So her mother immigrated from Bolivia and she moved to Miami, a place that's sort of overwhelmingly populated by people who fled socialist, communist regimes and really kind of
sentences.zh: 所以她的母亲从玻利维亚移民过来，搬到了迈阿密，一个几乎全是逃离社会主义、共产主义政权的人居住的地方，他们真的

sentences.en: see government involvement as a negative thing and want to have an economy based on pure capitalism and the free market.
sentences.zh: 把政府干预视为负面事物，并希望拥有一个基于纯粹资本主义和自由市场的经济。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。
